title: High Cols and Engraved Rock — Mercantour by Vésubie and Merveilles

bestPeriod.note: The cols above 2,400 m hold snow into early July and the CAF refuges close between mid and late September, after which there is no staffed water above the valleys.

summary: A two-base week in the southern Alps, running the Vésubie cirques and the Vallée des Merveilles with no lifts and no shortcuts.
hook: The Mercantour is an hour and a half from the Mediterranean and behaves nothing like it. Above Saint-Martin-Vésubie the valleys close into granite cirques with cold lakes, and over the watershed the Vallée des Merveilles holds thousands of Bronze Age engravings under Mont Bégo. There are no cable cars here. Every metre is earned, every bail-out is a valley path, and that is exactly why the trails are empty in August.

snapshot.Total Distance / Terrain: approx. 110–130 km, 6,000–7,000 m vert; granite slab, larch forest, scree, high lake basins
snapshot.Getting There: Nice (NCE) → Zou! regional bus to Saint-Martin-Vésubie, or the Nice–Tende railway to Saint-Dalmas-de-Tende for the Merveilles side
snapshot.Who It Suits: Self-sufficient mountain runners who want remoteness rather than infrastructure

itinerary.title: Le Boréon, gently
itinerary.morning: Arrive from Nice. If you are driving, take the Vésubie road up through Lantosque and Roquebillière and notice how much of it is new — the valley was rebuilt after the October 2020 floods and reconstruction is still visible.
itinerary.afternoon: Drive or ride 8 km up to Le Boréon (1,500 m) and run an easy loop: the lake, the Cascade du Boréon, and the forest track up the Vallon de Salèse under Norway spruce. Altitude adjustment, nothing more.
itinerary.evening: Back down to Saint-Martin-Vésubie. Walk the Rue du Docteur Cagnoli, the old street with a channel of spring water running down its middle, and fill your bottles from the fountains on the square.
itinerary.dayStats: 12 km, 450 m vert. Grade T1–T2, forest track and lakeside path, no exposure. Water: Le Boréon (Vacherie du Boréon, fountains), Saint-Martin-Vésubie fountains — all reliable year-round. Bail-out: the Boréon road runs to the trailhead.

itinerary.title: Les Lacs de Prals from La Madone de Fenestre
itinerary.morning: Drive the 12 km up the Vallon de la Madone to the sanctuary and the Refuge de la Madone de Fenestre (1,903 m), a stone chapel and CAF hut in a bare granite bowl. Climb the marked path east to the Cinq Lacs de Prals (2,270 m), five small tarns on a grassy shelf.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue to the Cime de la Valette de Prals for the view over the whole Vésubie, then descend the loop back to the Madone. Watch for flocks: this is patou country, and the descent path runs through summer grazing.
itinerary.evening: Eat in Saint-Martin. Trout, gnocchi, tourte de blettes — the Niçois mountain kitchen is heavier than the coast's.
itinerary.dayStats: 17 km, 900 m vert. Grade T2, grass, scree and slab; moderate exposure on the Valette ridge. Water: Refuge de la Madone de Fenestre, streams below the lakes (running until roughly late August, unreliable in September). Bail-out: the Madone road, with a hut at the trailhead.

itinerary.title: Recovery in the Boréon forest
itinerary.morning: Easy only. Run the forest tracks and the Vallon du Boréon path on soft larch duff, 60 minutes at conversational pace, no climbing above 1,800 m.
itinerary.afternoon: Visit Alpha, the wolf park at Le Boréon — wolves returned to the Mercantour in the 1990s and shape everything about how livestock is managed here, which in turn shapes the dogs you will meet on the trail.
itinerary.evening: Legs up. Tomorrow is the biggest day on the Vésubie side.
itinerary.dayStats: 11 km, 350 m vert. Grade T1, forest track. Water: Le Boréon. Bail-out: trivial.

itinerary.title: Cougourde, the Pas des Ladres and the Col de Fenestre
itinerary.morning: From Le Boréon climb the Vallon de la Cougourde to the Refuge de la Cougourde (2,090 m), under the granite tooth of the Cime de la Cougourde. Continue up to Lac de Trecolpas and over the Pas des Ladres (2,448 m).
itinerary.afternoon: Descend the far side to the Refuge de la Madone de Fenestre, refill, then climb north to the Col de Fenestre (2,474 m) on the Italian frontier — an old salt-trade pass with military ruins on the crest — and turn around. Return to Le Boréon over the Pas des Ladres, or arrange a pickup at the Madone road head to save 500 m of re-ascent.
itinerary.evening: Big meal, early night, and pack: you change valleys tomorrow.
itinerary.dayStats: 24–27 km, 1,600 m vert. Grade T2–T3; rocky, cairned sections near both cols, loose scree on the north side of the Ladres, moderate exposure. Water: Refuge de la Cougourde, Refuge de la Madone de Fenestre, Lac de Trecolpas outflow (reliable), and nothing at all on the Fenestre climb. Bail-out: descend to the Madone road head and the hut, which is staffed and has a phone.

itinerary.title: Over to the Roya, and easy legs at Castérino
itinerary.morning: The transfer. Drive east over the Col de Turini and down through Sospel and the Roya to Tende, then up the side road to Castérino (roughly 2h to 2h30 — this is a mountain road, do not underestimate it). Without a car, the alternative is the Nice–Tende railway and a taxi or seasonal shuttle up from Saint-Dalmas-de-Tende.
itinerary.afternoon: Shake the drive out on the Castérino valley track toward the Refuge de Valmasque, turning back at the first lake basin. Easy pace, 45–60 minutes.
itinerary.evening: Sort tomorrow's water and food in Castérino, which is a hamlet, not a town. Tende, 15 km below, has the shops.
itinerary.dayStats: 9 km, 300 m vert. Grade T1, jeep track and forest path. Water: Castérino hamlet, Refuge de Valmasque approach streams. Bail-out: single valley track.

itinerary.title: The Merveilles circuit under Mont Bégo
itinerary.morning: The big one, and the reason you came east. From Castérino climb the Vallon de la Valmasque past the Lac Vert and the Lac Noir to the Refuge de Valmasque (2,221 m), then up to the Baisse de Valmasque (2,549 m) on bare granite.
itinerary.afternoon: Drop south-west into the Vallée des Merveilles, past the Lac Long Supérieur and the Refuge des Merveilles (2,111 m). This is the archaeological core: thousands of Bronze Age petroglyphs on the ice-polished schist under Mont Bégo. Stay on the marked path — leaving it inside the engravings zone is prohibited without an accredited guide. Return to Castérino over the Pas de l'Arpette on the GR52.
itinerary.dayStats: 27–30 km, 1,500 m vert, 1,500 m descent. Grade T3 on the Baisse de Valmasque and the Arpette — cairned slab, scree, some hands-on rock; sustained exposure to weather above 2,200 m for four hours. Water: Refuge de Valmasque, Refuge des Merveilles, the lake outflows (reliable all season). Bail-out: both refuges are staffed in season; the Merveilles valley descends to the Lac des Mesches road head.

itinerary.title: Lac Vert at dawn, then the Train des Merveilles
itinerary.morning: Short and slow. Run the Valmasque track back up to the Lac Vert for the reflection at first light and come straight back down. Ninety minutes total.
itinerary.afternoon: Down to Tende. Walk the old town's stacked lanes, then take the Nice–Tende railway back to the coast — one of the great mountain railways in France, spiralling down the Roya in tunnels and viaducts.
itinerary.dayStats: 10 km, 400 m vert. Grade T1–T2, jeep track and stony path. Water: Castérino, Tende fountains. Bail-out: not needed.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotels and gîtes in Saint-Martin-Vésubie
accommodationStrategy.description: The only place in the valley with a pharmacy, a bakery, restaurants and a bus link to Nice, and it sits equidistant from the Boréon and Madone de Fenestre road heads — the two trailheads that carry four of this week's sessions. Ask for parking and a place to dry kit; and confirm the property's status, as some village stock was affected by the 2020 floods and rebuilding has been staged.

accommodationStrategy.name: Refuge de la Madone de Fenestre
accommodationStrategy.description: Worth one night if you want the Pas des Ladres and Col de Fenestre day to start at altitude instead of 900 m below it. Half-board, dormitories, cold running water and a guardian who knows the snow conditions on both cols better than any website. Book through the Club Alpin Français reservation system.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 4–6 weeks ahead; weekends in August go early.

accommodationStrategy.name: Gîtes and small hotels at Castérino
accommodationStrategy.description: Castérino is a scattering of buildings at the road head, which is precisely its value: the Merveilles circuit starts from the doorstep and you skip an hour of driving each way. Expect half-board, limited menu choice and no shop. Bring your own trail food from Tende.

logistics.emergency: 112. Mountain rescue in the Alpes-Maritimes is handled by the PGHM, based at Saint-Sauveur-sur-Tinée, and reached through 112. Coverage in the Valmasque and Fenestre cirques is patchy — expect to move to a col or ridge to get signal.
logistics.weather: Southern-Alps convection is violent and early. Storms can build by midday in August. Both big days should have you off the high ground by mid-afternoon.
logistics.money: Cards work in the villages; refuges vary and several are cash-preferred. Village shops close for a long lunch, roughly 12:30–15:00, and are shut on Sunday afternoons.

other.label: National park core-zone rules
other.text: Dogs are banned outright, even on a lead. Camping is banned; bivouac is tolerated only between 19:00 and 09:00 and at more than an hour's walk from the park boundary or a road. No fires, no drones, no picking anything, no leaving marked paths in the archaeological zone.

other.label: The Merveilles engravings zone
other.text: Off-path access requires an accredited guide. Rangers patrol in summer and the rule is enforced. The marked GR52 through the valley passes plenty of visible engravings — you do not need to leave it.

other.label: Patous
other.text: Livestock guardian dogs work these alpages unsupervised because wolves are present. If one comes at you: stop running, walk, keep your arms down, do not shout, do not swing poles, detour wide around the flock, and let the dog escort you out. Running through a flock is the one reliable way to get bitten.

other.label: Storm damage and trail status
other.text: Storm Alex in October 2020 destroyed roads, bridges and trails throughout the Vésubie and Roya. Much is rebuilt, some routes are still rerouted. Check the Parc national du Mercantour's trail-status page and the Saint-Martin-Vésubie tourist office before committing to a plan.

other.label: Water in late summer
other.text: The lakes and their outflows run all season; the grass-slope streams do not, and by September many are dry. The refuges are the reliable points, and they close from mid-September.

other.label: Roads
other.text: The Col de Turini and the Castérino side road are narrow, hairpinned and shared with cyclists and motorbikes at weekends. Budget more time than the map suggests.

proTips: Start the Day 4 and Day 6 loops before 07:00. The cols are the exposed part, the storms come in the afternoon, and this is a range where a single lift-served escape does not exist.

Run the Merveilles circuit anticlockwise — Valmasque first, Merveilles second. The Baisse de Valmasque is a steep granite climb best done fresh and in shade, and you then arrive at the engravings in the good afternoon light.

Ask the guardian at the Refuge de la Madone de Fenestre about the Pas des Ladres and Col de Fenestre before you go up. In early July they will tell you exactly which north-facing gully still holds hard snow.
Use the Nice–Tende railway as a one-way tool. It gets you to Saint-Dalmas-de-Tende and Tende without the Turini drive, and it means you can plan a point-to-point rather than a loop on your last day.
Refill at every refuge you pass, not at every second one. Between the Cougourde and the Madone there is nothing, and between the Baisse de Valmasque and the Merveilles refuge there is nothing.
Saint-Martin-Vésubie's street channel and square fountains are the cheapest and best water in the valley. Fill the night before rather than queuing at a refuge tap in the morning.
If the high cols are out, the Vallon de Salèse and the Col de Salèse give 700 m of gain on forest and alpage entirely below 2,050 m, and stay runnable in weather that shuts the cirques.

packingNotes: Shoes with a stiff midsole and real rock grip. Mercantour granite is abrasive and the scree above the cols is coarse and mobile.
2 L carrying capacity for the two big days. This is the single most important item on the list here.
A wind shell and a genuine waterproof — southern-Alps storms are short, violent and cold.
Light gloves and a warm layer: the Col de Fenestre and the Baisse de Valmasque sit near 2,500 m and hold wind.
Poles. Two 1,500 m days with no lift assistance, on scree, make them worth their weight.
High-factor sunscreen, a cap and proper sunglasses. This is 44° north at 2,400 m with granite and lake reflection.
Offline mapping plus a paper 1:25,000 of the Vallée des Merveilles. Cairned slab sections are easy to lose in cloud.
A survival blanket and a whistle — the standard alpine minimum, and here the rescue response is genuinely distant.
Cash for refuges, €40–€60, plus a card.
Insect repellent for the Boréon forest evenings and a tick tool; the lower larch woods have both.
whatCouldGoWrong: **A trail or road you planned on is still closed from flood damage.** Fallback: check the park's trail-status page the week before, and keep the Boréon–Salèse and Prals loops as substitutes since both are on the intact upper roads.

**Thunderstorm on the Baisse de Valmasque.** There is no shelter and no lift. Fallback: the Refuge de Valmasque and the Refuge des Merveilles bracket the col; commit to whichever is closer and wait it out rather than pushing over.
**A patou confronts you at speed on the Prals descent.** Fallback: stop, walk, and go wide. Plan the descent so you are not running blind into an alpage at 18:00 when the flock is being moved.

**Snow in the Pas des Ladres in early July.** North-facing and steep. Fallback: ask the Madone guardian, and if in doubt run the Cougourde and Trecolpas out-and-back instead, which stays below the col.

**You arrive after the refuges have closed for the season.** From roughly late September the huts shut, taking the water and the emergency shelter with them. Fallback: shift the trip earlier, or plan strictly valley-based days with full water carried from Saint-Martin-Vésubie.
